subject: research/sweep-twin
professional: a senior lidar-SLAM / state-estimation researcher (the kind who reviews motion-compensation and continuous-time odometry papers for ICRA/IROS or RA-L). They would check first that the closed forms match a simulation and an independent derivation, whether sign conventions hold under the spin/seam variants claimed, whether 'one scan reveals speed' is identifiable outside the toy room, and how the work relates to VICP, CT-ICP and scan-skew analyses

evidence.correctness: Independent numpy re-simulation (own vectorised ray cast into the rectangle, own fan selection via complex angle, SVD principal-axis line fit, numpy RNG with a different seed and 400 trials) reproduces every reported number: front/back wall 9.7500/-8.7500 and length bias 0.5000 at 10 m/s; tilts -0.9182/1.0232 deg and convergence 1.9414 deg (first order 2.0518) at 10 m/s, 3.7685 at 20 m/s; velocity inversion mean 9.821 sd 0.137 (-1.8%) at 10 m/s and 4.904 (-1.9%) at 5 m/s vs README 9.829/0.133 and 4.909; bearing bias by interpolating a simulated yaw sweep (36000 beams) -1.4100, -2.8199, -5.5528 deg = closed form -k beta/(1+k) (first-order -k beta would be 1.6-3% off, so the exact form matters); odometry bias 0.0500, -0.0750, 0.1250 = a tau/4 with scans placed in the world frame rather than by shifting the room; v_max = 2 tol/tau gives bias = tol. By hand: tilt at phi=0 from dx~/dphi = -v tau/2pi, dy~/dphi = x~ gives -v tau/(2 pi x~), consistent with the TLS results (front 9.75 m and back 8.75 m effective ranges; at 20 m/s both are 9.5 m, which is why front and back tilts coincide at 1.8843). One wrong closed form: length_bias returns s v tau/2, but for the paper's own clockwise configuration (phi0=+pi/2) the simulated bias is +0.5 m and the function returns -0.5 m; the sign depends on where the seam sits relative to the spin, not on spin alone. Not 4 because of that formula and because deskew-with-true-motion is exact by construction.

evidence.claims: Checked against files: items 1-6 numbers (results.txt and independent re-simulation, all pass), '12 tests, under 1 s' (pass), 'halving tau = halving v' (rows identical, pass), 'back wall 11% off' (1.1399 vs 1.0232: 11.4% of measured, 10.2% of first order, partial), backward driving 5% magnitude change (0.8735 vs 0.9182 = 4.9%, pass). Failed: whitepaper:11 'biased by exactly s v tau/2' with s the spin sign is wrong for the clockwise configuration the paper itself uses in item 2 (sim +0.50, formula -0.50). README:3 item (3) 'one scan reveals the speed' and research/README.md:234 'one scan gives speed to 0.13 m/s' omit the assumptions (truly parallel walls perpendicular to motion, known heading, no yaw) that whitepaper:13 states make it 'a consistency check, not an odometer'. README 'Builds on' names three CU Boulder groups with no paper reproduced: disclosed, but it is affiliation colour, not prior work. Disclaimer 'Stylised ... no measured scans' present.
evidence.fitness: Job: a researcher wanting to know how much a snapshot lidar simulator misleads a map or odometry pipeline. The scripted, reproducible closed forms are a decent teaching note and the yaw scale-error result is cleanly stated. But it is elementary rigid-body kinematics in a 2-D rectangle, and the nearest prior work is not cited: Hong, Ko & Kim (ICRA 2010) VICP estimates velocity inside ICP precisely to undo this distortion (the 'one scan reveals speed' idea in a general scene); Al-Nuaimi et al. (IPIN 2016) 'Analyzing LiDAR scan skewing and its impact on scan matching' quantifies the same skew and its effect on matching; Dellenbach et al. (ICRA 2022) CT-ICP and Park et al. (Elastic LiDAR Fusion, 2018) estimate intra-scan motion continuously; Ait-Aider et al. (ECCV 2006) recover object velocity from a single rolling-shutter view, the exact camera analogue. Only LOAM and Bosse & Zlot are cited; the third reference (sim-to-real RL survey) is tangential. Not part of a research/PROGRAMMES.md programme; well short of the PhD bar; new only as a compact worked example.
evidence.domain: Against lidar-odometry practice (per-point timestamps and IMU/constant-velocity deskew are standard in LOAM, LIO-SAM, FAST-LIO, CT-ICP): the 'deskew removes it to 1e-15 m' result is a tautology (inverse of the same model with the true motion); the practically important case, deskew with an estimated velocity, is listed as not simulated. The velocity estimator relies on a prior that walls are parallel, which a scan cannot distinguish from real wall convergence (disclosed in the whitepaper). The first-order inversion's -1.8% bias is reported rather than removed, though the exact x~ form is derived in the same paragraph. The length-bias sign convention is wrong for one spin/seam case. A practitioner would accept the kinematics and reject any transfer to hardware, as the author says.

verdict: A clean, reproducible 2-D kinematics note whose reported numbers are all right and one of whose closed forms is not. An independent numpy re-simulation reproduces every table value (length bias 0.5000 m, tilts -0.9182/1.0232 deg, convergence 1.9414 deg, velocity inversion 9.82 +- 0.14 m/s, bearing bias -k beta/(1+k) to four decimals, odometry bias a tau/4), and run.py and figure.py regenerate their committed outputs byte for byte. It misses the bar on verification, claims and the research gates: length_bias's `s v tau/2` gives -0.5 m where both simulators give +0.5 m for the clockwise setup the paper itself uses; 3 of 5 seeded mutants survive, including deleting yaw from the simulator; README states the single-scan speed result without the assumptions the whitepaper admits; and the nearest prior work (VICP, Al-Nuaimi 2016, CT-ICP, Ait-Aider 2006) is uncited, so a lidar-SLAM reviewer would read it as a worked example of known distortion, not a contribution.
